---
title: "Simulation Experiments"
subtitle: "From one model run to a small reproducible experiment"
toc: true
---

This chapter treats simulation as an empirical activity requiring deliberate design, reproducibility, and bounded interpretation.

## Planned learning outcomes

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

1. Initialize a fresh model instead of unknowingly continuing an earlier run.
2. Use the model's random-number generator and record a seed.
3. Run a model for a specified number of steps.
4. Collect agent-level and model-level measurements.
5. Recognize and inspect the resulting tabular data.
6. Plot an adoption trajectory.
7. Run multiple replications under the same parameter settings.
8. Vary one parameter systematically and compare the resulting distributions.
9. Distinguish a single illustrative trajectory from evidence about typical model behavior.
10. Explain how stochastic variation affects interpretation.
11. Document the model's mechanisms, assumptions, outputs, and limitations.
12. Make one principled modification and predict its consequences before running it.

## Planned scope

The experiment will compare repeated adoption trajectories across a small, predefined set of adoption-probability values. It will not introduce parallel computing, optimization, calibration to empirical data, or a network-based model.

## Culminating activity

The learner will design a small parameter comparison, run replications, create a plot or concise summary, interpret the stochastic results, and explain what the experiment cannot establish.
